```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 7  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [118, 190, 201, 99, 88]
    demands = [60, 39, 21, 21, 60, 17, 19]
    cost_matrix = [[21.12, 24.85, 28.47, 14.13, 10.68, 6.11, 20.84], [7.44, 6.73, 7.93, 21.28, 24.82, 26.68, 16.2], [11.85, 17.02, 21.75, 26.19, 29.52, 6.24, 17.67], [28.56, 12.46, 13.45, 21.35, 3.19, 3.58, 23.61], [28.11, 11.46, 15.36, 16.14, 14.97, 17.77, 11.17]]
    emission_matrix = [[1.2, 6.6, 1.74, 6.57, 4.09, 18.01, 15.35], [6.97, 6.31, 16.84, 13.62, 15.28, 11.26, 16.69], [5.56, 15.02, 6.79, 11.24, 1.0, 16.82, 9.34], [9.76, 13.27, 12.87, 8.82, 11.75, 20.0, 15.95], [5.31, 7.74, 12.46, 9.32, 5.74, 5.36, 3.99]]
    fixed_costs = [[193, 219, 149, 234, 208, 203, 259], [155, 278, 69, 128, 176, 75, 255], [185, 170, 161, 276, 230, 52, 65], [164, 109, 271, 229, 112, 153, 58], [257, 184, 250, 297, 198, 239, 112]]
    moq = [[10, 14, 11, 9, 16, 17, 7], [19, 15, 17, 9, 19, 18, 16], [13, 18, 6, 11, 15, 15, 5], [11, 20, 16, 16, 13, 11, 13], [5, 10, 8, 14, 13, 15, 5]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Supply Chain Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing Shipping Cost and Carbon with Real-World Operating Rules
Date: Today

Context
Our distribution network moves product from multiple warehouses to a broad set of stores. Each shipping route carries both a per-unit dollar cost and a per-unit CO2 emission rate. In many cases, the lowest-cost lanes are also the most carbon intensive. We need a shipping plan that reflects our financial discipline and our sustainability commitments without undermining service.

Operational Rules We Must Honor
- Route activation costs: Turning on any warehouse-to-store route requires a fixed setup charge that covers contracting, compliance, and dock readiness. This charge applies if we move any volume on that route, regardless of how much is shipped.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a route is activated, we must move at least a minimum number of units to justify transportation and handling. Partial loads are not accepted on active routes.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive deliveries from only a limited number of warehouses within a planning period. This cap protects receiving dock capacity, reduces vendor complexity, and aligns with existing commercial agreements.

Supply and Demand Realities
Each warehouse has finite available inventory for the period. Each store has a minimum demand that must be met to protect in-stock and sales. Our plan must allocate shipments without exceeding any warehouse’s available inventory while fully covering store requirements.

Management Priority on Cost vs. Emissions
Leadership has set relative importance weights for per-unit cost and per-unit emissions. We will evaluate each feasible plan using a blended measure that:
- Applies the cost weight to total variable shipping costs,
- Applies the emissions weight to total CO2 from shipments, and
- Adds the full setup charges for any activated routes without scaling them by the weights.
This approach formalizes the trade-off: a cheap but high-emission route will only be chosen when its cost advantage outweighs its weighted carbon impact, and vice versa.

Business Goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active route so that we:
- Do not exceed any warehouse’s available inventory,
- Meet or exceed each store’s minimum demand,
- Ship at least the required minimum on every activated route,
- Limit the number of supplying warehouses per store to the defined cap, and
- Achieve the lowest blended total of weighted variable shipping costs and weighted emissions, plus all setup charges for activated routes.

Deliverables and Next Steps
- A recommended list of active routes, with shipment quantities per active lane, expected financial spend, and expected carbon footprint under the stated priorities and operating rules.
- Sensitivity views that show how results shift when we adjust the cost and emission weights or tighten/relax the supplier cap.
- Implementation guidance for transportation scheduling, contract activation, and store receiving coordination to ensure the plan is executable in the field.
